correctness.rationale: Headline claim is a finite exact census proved by complete enumeration, not an inference from sampling. P=2*3*5*7*11*13=30030 and phi(P)=5760 verified arithmetically (1*2*4*6*10*12=5760). Two logically independent enumerations (gcd test vs boolean sieve striking 2,3,5,7,11,13) produce byte-identical ordered 5760-element coprime lists and histograms. Independent replay of inputs/artifacts/verify.py in this environment prints VERIFY_OK with HIST matching the table, SUM_N=5760, MOM=30030, MAX=22, N20=0, GAP22_STARTS [9439,20569]. Hand-checked moment identities: sum N = 1485+1485+1690+394+438+188+58+12+8+2 = 5760; sum d*N = 2970+5940+10140+3152+4380+2256+812+192+144+44 = 30030, telescopically forced to equal P. Parity (all gaps even) follows because P is even so all coprimes are odd, and was also exhaustively confirmed. Wrap gap (30030+1)-30029=2 is correctly included under the stated cyclic convention, and the linear-vs-cyclic one-count shift in N(2) is explicitly disclosed. Both 22-gap witnesses were machine-checked endpoint-coprime and interior-non-coprime, with exactly 2 occurrences. No essential inference, boundary condition, or computation is unverified. Finite-verification proof is correctly distinguished from any asymptotic or experimental claim; no larger-primorialion is asserted.

originality.rationale: Nearest priors were fetched live and compared substantively (not by timestamp). (1) Ziller arXiv:2007.01808 abstract states 'Existence and frequency of these numbers have not yet been clarified'; full text (Table 1 discussion) gives for k=6 only Nmin=18, non-existent {20}, h=22, plus bound 2k<=Nmin and conjecture h(k-1)<=Nmin(k) — occurrence data only, no per-gap frequencies. (2) OEIS A331118 row 6 is the union {2,4,6,8,10,12,14,16,18,22} (missing 20); comments say 'We take the union of the first differences' and Mathematica uses Union@s, which discards multiplicities by construction — occurrence set only. (3) OEIS A048670 a(6)=22 is the Jacobsthal maximum only. (4) Ziller-Morack arXiv:1611.03310 computes Jacobsthal maxima plus exhaustive maximum-length sequences in ancillaries — extremal gaps only, not the full 5760-gap spectrum. (5) OEIS A286941 publishes raw totative rows (from which a histogram is computable) but records no gap histogram; an OEIS search for '1485,1485,1690' returns no results, confirming the frequency vector is not tabled. Maxima, unions, raw ordered lists, and single extremal witnesses do not logically imply the 11-entry multiplicity vector with its two moment constraints. The new invariant (full N_6(d) distribution with N(20)=0) directly answers the explicitly open 'frequency' half at this scope.

value.rationale: Strongest headline claim judged on its own: first complete consecutive-coprime gap-frequency census at P6=30030 with proved unique missing even 20 and two located 22-gaps. Object and invariant were motivated before computation by Ziller (2020), which explicitly leaves frequency unclarified and conjectures all evens up to h(k-1) occur. P6 is a natural benchmark, not an arbitrary slice: smallest primorial row exhibiting a missing even (Nmin=18<Nmax=22) and largest small-primorial period fully enumerable in seconds (5760 gaps). Value is not known (no checked source records N(d)) and not mechanically implied by a max or union. A future researcher calibrating primorial k-tuple/Hardy-Littlewood density heuristics or quantitatively testing the h(k-1) occurrence conjecture can reasonably need these exact counts, witnesses, and moment audits as a citable benchmark. This is the eligible narrow-exact-invariant case: one benchmark distribution with stated limitations, not a general theorem, and presentation honestly claims no larger-primorial result. It is not a textbook restatement, parameter substitution (distribution replaces maximum/union), tiny unmotivated gain, or unexplained enumeration.

decisive_checks: Replayed inputs/artifacts/verify.py in audit environment: VERIFY_OK, HIST matches table, SUM_N=5760, MOM=30030, MAX=22, N20=0, GAP22_STARTS [9439,20569]; dual enumeration (gcd vs sieve) byte-identical.
Hand-verified sum N(d)=5760 and first-moment sum d*N(d)=30030 from the table; phi(30030)=5760 via 1*2*4*6*10*12.
Confirmed parity argument (P even => all coprimes odd => all gaps even) and cyclic-wrap disclosure; verified 30029 coprime to P so wrap gap is 2.
Confirmed union-vs-frequency distinction on A331118 page (Union@s) and occurrence-only content of Ziller Table 1 and A048670 maximum; numeric OEIS search for the count vector is empty.
residual_risks: Computation-based proof: correctness rests on seconds-scale exhaustive code replayed here; latent hardware/std-lib faults are negligible but the certificate should be re-run by any reuser (replay is seconds-scale).

Literature search is bounded to the nearest explicit priors plus a numeric-sequence check; an obscure tabulation of the same 11 counts elsewhere cannot be logically excluded, but no such source was found and the open-frequency statement plus empty numeric search make it unlikely.

Raw totative list (A286941 row 6) makes the histogram re-derivable in seconds; novelty rests on the substantive union-vs-frequency gap and the explicitly open frequency question, not on computational difficulty.
Single-benchmark scope: census covers P6=30030 only under the cyclic-gap convention; linear (non-cyclic) reading shifts N(2) to 1484 over 5759 gaps, as disclosed.
